title: Resveratrol Promotes Goat Myoblast Differentiation via PROX1-Mediated Inhibition of NOTCH Signaling.
authors: Wei, Yirong; Liu, Yufan; Wu, Shaoqiang; Xu, Dinghao; Cheng, Pengfei; Huang, Yanna; Jiang, Qinyang
one_liner_zh: 研究白藜芦醇通过PROX1抑制NOTCH信号促进山羊成肌细胞分化，仅含分子对接且非蛋白-DNA互作核心，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic compound, has been reported to regulate cellular differentiation; however, its role in skeletal muscle development in ruminants remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which RES regulates myoblast differentiation in goats, with a focus on the role of PROX1 and its downstream signaling pathways. METHODS: Primary myoblasts isolated from a 3-mo-old fetal Nubian goat were used as an in vitro model and treated with 20 mumol/L RES, with untreated cells serving as controls. RNA sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes, and RT-qPCR, molecular docking, as well as gain- and loss-of-function assays were conducted to investigate the role of PROX1 in myogenic differentiation. For in vivo validation, 20 healthy castrated male Nubian goats (180 +/- 3 d of age; n = 10/group) were fed either a basal diet (CON) or a basal diet supplemented with 150 mg/kg RES for 120 d. Longissimus dorsi muscle samples were collected at the end of the experiment for subsequent analyses. Myogenic markers and signaling pathways were analyzed, and relative gene expression was calculated using the 2(-DeltaDeltaCt) method. RESULTS: RNA-seq identified 221 differentially expressed genes after RES treatment, among which PROX1 was significantly upregulated (Log2Fold Change = 1.7,  approximately 3.25-fold compared with control, P < 0.0001). Molecular docking analysis indicated a stable interaction between RES and PROX1. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments showed that RES significantly increased PROX1 expression by  approximately 182% and 105%, respectively (P < 0.001). Functional analyses demonstrated that PROX1 overexpression promoted myogenic differentiation, increasing the mRNA expression levels of MyoD, MyoG, and MyHC to 2.70-, 1.75-, and 1.80-fold of control levels, respectively (P < 0.001), whereas MyoD protein expression increased by  approximately 80% (P < 0.001) and myotube formation was significantly enhanced (P < 0.001). In contrast, PROX1 knockdown markedly inhibited myogenic differentiation, reducing the mRNA expression of MyoD, MyoG, and MyHC by 75%, 48%, and 51%, respectively (P < 0.05), and decreasing MyoD protein expression by  approximately 43% (P < 0.001). Mechanistically, PROX1 promoted myogenic differentiation through suppression of the NOTCH1/HES1 signaling pathway (P < 0.05). Moreover, RES partially rescued the differentiation impairment induced by PROX1 deficiency through activation of PROX1 (P < 0.05). In vivo validation yielded results consistent with those observed in vitro. CONCLUSIONS: RES promotes myoblast differentiation in goats through PROX1 activation and modulation of NOTCH signaling. These findings identify a PROX1-associated regulatory mechanism in skeletal muscle development in goats.
abstract_zh: 背景：白藜芦醇（Resveratrol, RES）是一种天然多酚类化合物，已有报道称其可调控细胞分化；然而，其在反刍动物骨骼肌发育中的作用仍不清楚。目的：本研究旨在阐明RES调控山羊成肌细胞分化的分子机制，重点关注PROX1及其下游信号通路的作用。方法：从3月龄胎儿努比亚山羊中分离的原代成肌细胞作为体外模型，用20 μmol/L RES处理，未处理细胞作为对照。进行RNA测序以鉴定差异表达基因，并采用RT-qPCR、分子对接以及功能获得和功能丧失实验研究PROX1在肌源性分化中的作用。体内验证中，20只健康去势雄性努比亚山羊（180 ± 3日龄；每组n = 10）分别饲喂基础日粮（CON）或添加150 mg/kg RES的基础日粮，持续120 d。实验结束时采集背最长肌样本用于后续分析。分析肌源性标志物和信号通路，相对基因表达采用2^(-ΔΔCt)方法计算。结果：RNA-seq在RES处理后鉴定出221个差异表达基因，其中PROX1显著上调（Log2Fold Change = 1.7，约为对照的3.25倍，P < 0.0001）。分子对接分析表明RES与PROX1之间存在稳定相互作用。体外和体内实验均显示，RES显著提高PROX1表达，分别约为182%和105%（P < 0.001）。功能分析表明，PROX1过表达促进肌源性分化，使MyoD、MyoG和MyHC的mRNA表达水平分别增至对照的2.70、1.75和1.80倍（P < 0.001），而MyoD蛋白表达增加约80%（P < 0.001），肌管形成显著增强（P < 0.001）。相反，PROX1敲低显著抑制肌源性分化，使MyoD、MyoG和MyHC的mRNA表达分别降低75%、48%和51%（P < 0.05），并使MyoD蛋白表达减少约43%（P < 0.001）。机制上，PROX1通过抑制NOTCH1/HES1信号通路促进肌源性分化（P < 0.05）。此外，RES通过激活PROX1部分挽救PROX1缺乏引起的分化损伤（P < 0.05）。体内验证结果与体外观察一致。结论：RES通过PROX1激活和NOTCH信号调控促进山羊成肌细胞分化。这些发现揭示了山羊骨骼肌发育中一个与PROX1相关的调控机制。
